All acceptance criteria for Story 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS are implemented and verified: - Core functionality: valid-annotation-format now accepts both nested (story.pattern/req.pattern) and flat (storyPathPattern/requirementIdPattern) configuration for story paths and requirement IDs. - Backward compatibility: when no patterns are configured, the rule uses the previous hardcoded defaults; when invalid patterns are provided, it reports configuration errors and safely falls back to defaults while still validating annotations. - Pattern validation: custom patterns are compiled into RegExp with robust error handling; invalid regex sources generate precise "invalidRuleConfiguration" diagnostics. - Error messages: optional example strings (nested and flat) are respected and appear in diagnostics; nested examples override flat ones as documented. - Quality/schema: rule meta.schema is driven by a dedicated JSON Schema builder that constrains all new options and disallows unknown fields, aligning with ESLint best practices. - Integration: configurable pattern behavior coexists with valid-story-reference’s storyDirectories-based path resolution; defaults are aligned and the full suite (including both rules) passes, indicating no integration regressions. - Documentation: the valid-annotation-format rule documentation has been updated with clear examples and explanations for both nested and flat configuration forms, matching the story’s described use cases.
On this basis, the story is fully implemented and verified by tests and documentation, so the status is PASSED.
